answer: The wander multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and sonnet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 679 identities would post 1588 proofs and burn roughly 48 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
